claims.claim: Phantom reads cannot occur at either level in PostgreSQL; serialization anomalies are possible at Repeatable Read and impossible at Serializable
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Both levels can raise errors that prevent serialization anomalies, so applications must be ready to retry; the SQLSTATE is 40001 serialization_failure
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Retrying deadlocks (40P01) may be advisable; unique (23505) and exclusion (23P01) violations are sometimes worth retrying but need more care because they may be persistent errors
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Retry the complete transaction including its decision logic; PostgreSQL has no automatic retry; a retry is not guaranteed to succeed and may take many attempts
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: At Repeatable Read, modifying or locking a row that another transaction changed and committed causes 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: In the docs' class-sum example both transactions commit at Repeatable Read, and at Serializable one fails with a read/write dependencies error
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Serializable uses non-blocking predicate locks (SSI) that cannot cause deadlocks; it blocks only for SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Unique-constraint violations can still occur between overlapping Serializable transactions after an existence check, so 23505 is sometimes worth retrying
claims.label: partial

sibyl.notes: Claims citing the failure-handling page are well supported. The transaction-iso excerpt contains only the isolation table, so the behavioral claims cited to it (error messages, example, predicate locks) are unsupported. The answer discloses that claims 5-9 lack verified quotes, but they are still material. Claim 9 (read-only retry behavior) was not extracted because of the 8-claim cap. The answer says it did not search for counterevidence, but it discloses its limits and includes the unique-violation caveat.

claims.claim: Repeatable Read sees a snapshot taken at the first non-transaction-control statement
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: At Repeatable Read, modifying or locking a row that a concurrent transaction updated or deleted gives 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Repeatable Read is not guaranteed to match any serial execution, so enforcing business rules needs explicit locks
claims.label: partial

claims.claim: Serializable is Repeatable Read plus monitoring for read/write dependencies, and it rolls one transaction back with a read/write dependencies error
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Serialization failures always carry SQLSTATE 40001 serialization_failure, and the message text varies
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Serialization failures always carry SQLSTATE 40001 serialization_failure, and the message text varies
claims.label: partial

claims.claim: Retry the complete transaction including its decision logic; PostgreSQL has no automatic retry because it cannot guarantee correctness
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Retry 40001 unconditionally; 40P01 retries may be advisable; 23505 and 23P01 are sometimes appropriate to retry but need care because they may be persistent
claims.label: supported

deep_research.notes: The retry guidance is fully supported by the failure-handling page. The errcodes page confirms only the 40001 code-to-name mapping, not the 'always' or 'message varies' parts. The mechanism claims cited to transaction-iso (snapshot timing, error messages, monitoring, predicate locks, unique violations, read-only nuance) are not in the table-only excerpt. The answer discloses that it relied on summarized retrieval and notes the read-only and unique-violation caveats.

claims.claim: Repeatable Read uses one snapshot taken at the first non-transaction-control statement, so successive SELECTs see the same data
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Serializable works like Repeatable Read plus monitoring for conditions inconsistent with every serial execution
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: In PostgreSQL, Repeatable Read prevents dirty, nonrepeatable and phantom reads but allows serialization anomalies, which Serializable also prevents
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: In the class-sum example both transactions commit under Repeatable Read, and under Serializable one is rolled back
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Repeatable Read fails with a 'concurrent update' error; Serializable can fail with a 'read/write dependencies' error
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Applications at either level must be prepared to retry by rerunning the whole transaction from the beginning
claims.label: unsupported

claims.claim: Serialization failures carry SQLSTATE 40001 serialization_failure, and the docs recommend retrying them unconditionally
claims.label: supported

claims.claim: Retrying 40P01 deadlock_detected may also be advisable
claims.label: supported

native.notes: The table claim and the failure-handling claims are supported. Later failure-handling claims (23505/23P01 retries, complete-transaction retry, no guarantee of success) are also supported but fell outside the 8-claim cap. The retry claim cited to transaction-iso is stated on the failure-handling page, not in the table-only excerpt. The snapshot, monitoring, example and error-message claims are unsupported by the excerpt. The answer cautiously declines to extend the read-only claim to Serializable and drops the unverified unique-violation claim, which is disclosed limitation rather than substantive counterevidence.
